subject: MSA/IP boundary — proposed operational guardrails
body:
From: Mike Chen <mike.chen@acmetech.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@acmetech.com
Date: 2025-09-03 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: training consent & derivative use for MSA

Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal asked us to surface one last set of questions before we finalize the order form and MSA:

1) Will AcmeTech outputs be treated as customer-owned for productization purposes? We need explicit language saying AcmeTech can use outputs to build internal products.
2) Will Redwood include a training/feedback license that permits model improvements on customer data? If so, can Acme opt-out or require anonymization?

We aim to sign this week; appreciate a short answer and any proposed contract language.

Regards,
Mike Chen
Head of Procurement
AcmeTech

---

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@acmetech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-03 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: training consent & derivative use for MSA

Mike —

Short answers up front:
- Output/productization: we can grant AcmeTech broad rights to use outputs for internal products and customer-facing features.
- Training/feedback: our standard is a limited feedback license used to improve service quality; customers can opt out via the order form, and we can commit to not training on PII or uploaded proprietary data unless explicitly permitted.

I've looped in Ben (AE) to align on commercial terms and Laura (legal) to attach a redline with our recommended language. If Acme needs a hard opt-out checkbox in the order form, we can add it and reflect the pricing delta.

Next steps:
- Laura to circulate redlines for MSA + order form (expect in the next message).
- Ben will confirm pricing impact for opt-out.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

---

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@acmetech.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-03 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood redline: training/outputs (MSA v3)
Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.docx (docx)

Mike —

Attached is our redline to the MSA with specific clauses called out:
- Section 4.2 (Customer Outputs): clear grant back for AcmeTech to use outputs internally and externally.
- Section 7.1 (Feedback & Training License): a limited, revocable license allowing Redwood to use non-PII, de-identified usage data for model improvement; explicit opt-out mechanics in the order form.
- New Schedule B (Data Safeguards): binding commitments around PII exclusion, retention windows, and audit rights.

Key compromise points: if Acme elects to opt out of training use, we propose a 15% uplift on per-token pricing to cover the lost signal across shared models. That uplift is negotiable depending on volume.

Please review and tell us where you'd like to trade leverage.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

---

From: Sasha Petrov <sasha.petrov@acmetech.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@acmetech.com>, contracts@acmetech.com
Date: 2025-09-04 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood redline: training/outputs (MSA v3)
Attachments: AcmeTech_ACORD_redlines_20250902.pdf (pdf)

Laura / Tessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear structure. A few points from Acme legal after an internal review:

- Outputs: Acme needs an unconditional right to create derivative internal and customer-facing products from model outputs. We want language that prevents Redwood from asserting ownership over the output artifacts that Acme ships.
- Training license: Acme will not accept a right for Redwood to train on any data that includes Acme customer content unless we expressly permit it. We can consider a narrowly scoped telemetry signal (aggregated, rate-limited metrics) but not raw tokens.
- Opt-out pricing: the proposed 15% uplift is acceptable as a starting point; we want that expressed as a fixed schedule and capped for 12 months following execution.

We have attached our annotated redline (AcmeTech_ACORD_redlines_20250902.pdf). Our outside counsel would prefer to keep training permission out of the MSA and instead require a separate addendum if Acme decides to opt in later.

Happy to hop on a quick call to align.

Best,
Sasha Petrov
Sr. Counsel — IP & Privacy
AcmeTech

---

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@acmetech.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-04 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood redline: training/outputs (MSA v3)

Thanks Sasha — appreciate the clarity. Two quick commercial notes:
- If Acme opts out of training, the 15% uplift would apply to the baseline hosted rates; if volumes exceed the initial commitment we can revisit the cap earlier.
- We can commit to a 12-month cap on the uplift as requested.

If legal wants the training permission out of the MSA and in an opt-in addendum, that's operationally fine, but we'd prefer a short placeholder in the MSA that references the addendum so both teams know where to look later.

I'll coordinate internally on implementation and timeline; Tessa / Laura — can you confirm if the placeholder language is acceptable?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Sasha Petrov <sasha.petrov@acmetech.com>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@acmetech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-05 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood redline: training/outputs (MSA v3) — next steps

Sasha / Mike —

Thanks — this is helpful and we're close. Proposed path forward:
1) Redwood and Acme agree to keep training permissions out of the core MSA; we will add a one-line placeholder in §7 acknowledging an optional "Training Addendum" (no rights granted by default).
2) We will deliver a clean order form with a clear opt-out checkbox and the uplift schedule (15% cap for 12 months) so procurement can sign immediately.
3) If Acme wants to opt in later, we'll execute the separate Training Addendum that defines permitted telemetry (aggregated metrics only unless Acme gives explicit written consent).

Action items:
- Laura: finalize the MSA placeholder and attach updated redline (cc'd).
- Ben: produce a clean order form with the opt-out checkbox and revised pricing schedule by EOD Friday.
- Sasha/Mike: confirm acceptance of the path above so we can get DocuSign out.

If that sounds good I can prepare the DocuSign envelope and route it for signatures.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

(Attachment stubs referenced above: Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.docx — summary redline; AcmeTech_ACORD_redlines_20250902.pdf — Acme's annotated comments.)
